speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash, such as whether it consists of bumps, blisters, or flat red spots, and has it started on your face or trunk before spreading? Also, have you been in contact with anyone who has had chickenpox or shingles recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the facial rash spread downwards to the trunk and extremities in a descending pattern, and do the lesions appear as raised, red spots that look like drops of water on rose petals? Are you currently experiencing any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a descending rash on the trunk and extremities, accompanied by low-grade fever and headache, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
